title: nolan sets up nolan
$comment: The meta-demo: nolan filming the real experience of using nolan — setup, then the actual mechanic (a screenplay + a style, invoked from one command, echoing the build with beats/pace/seconds), then it films your real app, then the finished GIF. nolan only films web pages, so the terminal is a mock (examples/site/setup.html) that nolan types into and `call submit` commits; the terminal `cat`/echo output is the REAL screenplay/style/CLI output (this demo must not fake what nolan does). The 'real app' scene is the actual toy app (index.html); the result scene (done.html) shows a real nolan GIF. Avoids the purple `pill` style. Film with --style=examples/metademo.style.json (presenter ~20% smaller).

beats.text: nolan is a screenplay, a style, and one command. Here's all of it.
git clone https://github.com/richardofortune/nolan && cd nolan && npm install

args: Cloning… installing dependencies… Playwright + Chromium ready ✓

beats.text: Cloned, with a real browser to film in.
The screenplay is WHAT happens — an agent can write it.
The style is HOW it looks — and how fast.

beats.text: One command, and nolan narrates the build — beats, pace, seconds.
That "filming" line? This is it — driving your real app.
Move the UI and it fails CI — nolan verify catches the drift.
Out comes a GIF — the same beats, the same seconds, every release.
Show, don't tell. This demo just set nolan up to make itself.
